title: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale
abstract: arXiv:2610.31439v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Given an unseen graph, a start node, $s$, and an end node, $t$, can a language model generate the shortest path from $s$ to $t$? Prior work has found that models fail to learn this task as the graphs scale. We show that this failure has two causes: the supervision signal and the tokenization. First, we theoretically establish and empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of multi-token prediction (MTP), and show that the benefits of MTP are topologically agnostic. Second, we introduce alternative tokenizations and show that the two causes are orthogonal. Using these methods, we break through the scaling wall observed by prior work, consistently and stably learning to solve the task at scales far beyond previous limits.

translated_title: 多Token预测与替代分词方法提升大规模潜在多跳图搜索的学习能力
translated_abstract: 给定一个未见过的图、一个起始节点 $s$ 和一个终止节点 $t$，语言模型能否生成从 $s$ 到 $t$ 的最短路径？先前的研究发现，随着图规模的扩大，模型无法学会这一任务。我们证明这种失败有两个原因：监督信号和分词方式。首先，我们从理论上建立并从实证上证明了多Token预测（MTP）的有效性，并表明MTP的益处与图的拓扑结构无关。其次，我们引入了替代分词方法，并证明这两个原因是相互正交的。利用这些方法，我们突破了先前研究观察到的规模瓶颈，在远超以往极限的规模上持续且稳定地学习解决该任务。
tldr: 本文指出模型难以学习大规模图上最短路径搜索的两个原因——监督信号与分词方式，并提出多Token预测和替代分词这两种相互正交的方法，突破了以往工作的规模瓶颈。
en_tdlr: Multi-token prediction and alternative tokenization—two orthogonal improvements addressing the supervision signal and tokenization—enable language models to stably learn latent multi-hop graph search at scales far beyond previous limits.
